cover.caption: Svir det, er det fisken som biter.
cover.alt: Bjørnen sitter ute på isen mellom tre isfiskere på bøtter og har halen nede i et hull. Isfiskerne stirrer på ham. Langt bak på parkeringsplassen lusker reven av sted med fiskeposen sin.

Far behind him, in the parking lot between high snowbanks, the Fox slips away with his plastic bag of fish. The ice fishers stare at him.

- the Bear: A huge, heavy, slow-moving and rather sleepy brown bear, taller than a man when he stands up, with thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose and a patient, slightly puzzled look. Story world: Present-day Norway in late November and December, where a bear and a fox live among people and talk. Below a spruce forest lies the Frozen Lake, a small lake frozen since late November, with ice fishers hunched on plastic buckets over their holes. The bear and the fox are wild animals without clothes: they walk on four legs, but can sit up and use their front paws like hands.

characters.name: Bjørnen

characters.name: Den stubbrumpete bjørnen
characters.description: Bjørnen etter isfisket, med bare en liten stump igjen bak. Han bærer ikke nag, han utsetter dvalen til over nyttår for julesmørets skyld, og han liker ting som er rettferdige.
characters.look: The same huge, heavy, slow-moving and rather sleepy brown bear after his fishing trip: thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, a patient, slightly puzzled look and enormous flat paws with blunt claws. illustrations.anchor: Bjørnen sto på parkeringsplassen og så på dem
illustrations.caption: «Jeg har vært og fisket, jeg», sa reven.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated book of modern fairy tales, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Late afternoon on the Sunny Slope, long blue shadows on the snow. The Stub-tailed Bear has just woken and twists round to look at his own backside, which glistens with a thin, shiny coat of melted butter. The Fox sits up beside him, pointing at it with one paw and a solemn, sorry face. The empty butter tub stands in the snow next to them as evidence.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Stub-tailed Bear: The same huge, heavy, slow-moving and rather sleepy brown bear after his fishing trip: thick, shaggy dark chocolate-brown winter fur, a broad head with small round ears, small, gentle black eyes under heavy brows, a short greyish-tan muzzle with a big black nose, a patient, slightly puzzled look and enormous flat paws with blunt claws. His long tail is gone: all that is left is a tiny, round, fluffy stump on his big round bottom.
- the Fox: A slim, light-footed, long-legged red fox with sleek, bright flame-red winter fur, a snow-white chin, throat and chest, black lower legs and paws, tall pointed ears with black backs, narrow amber eyes with a sly sideways glance, a long pointed snout with long whiskers and a smooth, self-confident grin. His big, bushy red tail ends in a clean white tip.

Setting:
- the Sunny Slope: A south-facing slope at the edge of the spruce forest above the lake, where the low December sun shines: smooth, sparkling snow, a few grey rocks and tufts of dry golden grass, and at the top one dense, dark spruce whose low branches sweep the snow, with a hollow underneath. Through the trees below, glimpses of the frozen lake and the parking lot.

Story world: Present-day Norway in late November and December, where a bear and a fox live among people and talk. Below a spruce forest lies the Frozen Lake, a small lake frozen since late November, with ice fishers hunched on plastic buckets over their holes. By the shore there is a ploughed gravel parking lot with high snowbanks, a small grocery shop, and on Thursdays a white fish van. Up at the edge of the forest is the Sunny Slope, with one dense spruce at the top. The fox's fish are neatly bundled and packed in a plastic bag. The butter is one round yellow plastic tub with a snap-on lid and no readable label. The bear and the fox are wild animals without clothes: they walk on four legs, but can sit up and use their front paws like hands.

This story's season, light and colours: Late November to just before Christmas: short, grey-blue days over a white frozen lake, with the warm orange glow of the shop window and headlights in the parking lot; then a clear, cold December day of low, golden sun on the snowy slope and long blue shadows. Accents: the fox's flame red, butter yellow and dark spruce green.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Every character has their own face, build, age, hair and clothes exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Dry humour, careful composition with one focal point and plenty of negative space. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.
